iflow.configuration.nodePath.description: Node.js executable used to start the Core. Leave empty to find a suitable Node.js automatically; you normally do not need to change this, and only set it when detection fails or you need a specific version.
iflow.configuration.warmStart.descriptio: Start the Core in the background when the window opens, so the chat panel is ready the first time you open it. Costs about 100 MB of memory per window. On by default.
iflow.configuration.soundFeedback.descri: Play a short sound when a turn finishes or fails, even while the panel is not in the foreground. On by default.
iflow.configuration.auroraIntensity.desc: Opacity of the aurora light spots behind the panel; higher values make them more visible. Default 35, range 0–100 (0 hides them entirely).
iflow.configuration.theme.description: Panel color theme: auto follows the current VSCode color theme, light pins a light theme, dark pins a dark theme. Stored in your user settings, so VSCode Settings Sync can carry it to other machines. Default auto.
iflow.configuration.uiFontSize.descripti: Text size in the panel: compact (11 px baseline), standard (about 12 px, the default), or large (about 13 px). Affects the panel only, not the editor font size.
iflow.configuration.uiDensity.descriptio: Spacing in the panel: compact, standard (the default), or comfortable. Changes padding and gaps only, not text size.
iflow.configuration.restoreLastSession.d: Reopen the session you used last when the panel starts instead of starting a new one. Falls back to a new session when nothing can be restored. Off by default.
iflow.configuration.autoOpenPanel.descri: Open the chat panel automatically when VSCode starts. Off by default.
iflow.configuration.language.description: Interface language for the Core, saved to your local iFlow configuration. Leave empty to keep the Core's current language. Takes effect after a Core restart.
iflow.configuration.superAgentIntegratio: How a finished child session's changes are brought back into your working tree: `merge` (the default) merges its branch into the current branch automatically — the merge is previewed first, so it only steps aside (with a notice) when it would overwrite your uncommitted changes or a merge is already in progress, and conflicts are detected before anything is written; `pr` pushes the branch and opens a pull request (requires the gh CLI); `manual` keeps the branch for you to merge from the child-session board. Child sessions always run without tool approvals.
iflow.configuration.superAgentMaxConcurr: How many child sessions may run at the same time. Extra dispatches queue in order and start as slots free up; lowering the limit does not interrupt sessions already running. Default 5, range 1–20; applies immediately.
iflow.configuration.superAgentMaxAttempt: How many times a failed child session is attempted automatically, including the first attempt. 1 means no automatic retry; the default is 2, range 1–5. Takes effect on the next child session that starts.
iflow.configuration.superAgentDependency: What happens to a child session whose upstream task failed: `block` (the default) skips the dependent task and marks it as blocked, while `continue` runs the dependent task anyway.
**Full trust mode** (off by default). When enabled, child sessions run directly in the main repository workspace with no worktree isolation, keep all built-in tools and all broker-proxied MCP servers, and may push, open pull requests and merge in the main repository. WARNING: in full trust mode child sessions can modify main-repository files, run arbitrary commands and push/open PRs — only enable it for tasks you fully trust.
iflow.configuration.superAgentKeepWorktr: Whether a child session's working directory is kept after it finishes normally. Off by default: the directory is deleted and its branch is always kept. Turn it on to keep the directory too, so you can keep editing by hand. Failed or interrupted child sessions always keep their directory so a retry resumes the exact state. Applies to the next child session that finishes.
iflow.configuration.superAgentMaxWorktre: How many finished child-session working directories to keep on disk. When the limit is exceeded, the oldest are removed first (by last modification time) and branches are always kept for your review; directories with uncommitted changes are never removed. Default 10, range 0–100 (0 = no limit).
iflow.configuration.superAgentChildToolA: Restrict which built-in tools a child session may use, by tool name (for example `read_file`, `run_shell_command`). Leave empty (default) to keep all tools available. When set, only the listed tools are registered in the child — this is a hard structural gate, so list every tool the child needs, including `task` for in-process sub-agents. Applies to the next child session that starts.
iflow.configuration.superAgentChildMcpSe: Restrict which MCP servers a child session may reach, by server name as shown in the child-session board's MCP status. Leave empty (default) to keep the current behavior (all broker-proxied servers). When set, only servers that both appear here and are actually available from the host broker are exposed to the child; names not present in the broker are ignored. Applies to the next child session that starts.
iflow.configuration.osNotifications.desc: Send OS notifications while the panel is not visible: approvals (the default) only when an approval or a question needs you, all also when a turn finishes, off disables them. Child-session reports are not announced one by one — you are notified only when a child session asks you a question, and when all child sessions have finished.
iflow.configuration.contextWindowOverrid: Override model context-window sizes, one per line as model=tokenCount (for example glm-4.6=200000). The model name may include or omit the provider prefix — auto/deepseek-v4.1-flash and deepseek-v4.1-flash are the same entry. The value must be a plain token number: 960K is not parsed and that entry is silently dropped. Leave empty (or leave a model out) to use that model's default window. An entry takes precedence over the built-in table and over the active profile's limit, and is pushed to the CLI so its auto-compression threshold matches the window shown in the panel.
iflow.configuration.costTable.descriptio: Unit prices used for the session cost estimate, one per line as model=inputPrice,outputPrice in USD per million tokens (for example deepseek-v3=0.27,1.1). Affects only the cost shown in the panel, never actual billing.
iflow.configuration.thinkingModelRules.d: Rules that decide which models support thinking (reasoning). Each entry has pattern (a case-insensitive regex matched against the model name, first match wins), supportsThinking, and optionally supportedReasoningLevels and maxThinkingTokens (0 = the Core's default). Built-in defaults cover mainstream thinking models; entries you write by hand in your local iFlow configuration are never overwritten. When a model's rule sets supportsThinking to false, its reasoning-level dropdown is greyed out. Applies from the next session start.
iflow.configuration.autoTitle.descriptio: After a session's first turn, generate a short AI title for it in the session list. One extra lightweight model call per session. On by default.
After each turn, make one extra model call to guess your likely next steps and show them as chips above the composer. Uses extra tokens. On by default.
iflow.configuration.autoCompressOnIdle.d: After a turn finishes, if context occupancy has reached the threshold (see Auto-compress threshold, 95% by default), compress the conversation before the next turn. Off by default; a context-overflow error from the gateway still triggers compression.
iflow.configuration.autoMemoryCapture.de: After each turn, use the current model to extract preferences and conventions worth keeping as candidates. Nothing is written until you confirm, so memories are never saved silently. On by default; uses extra tokens.
iflow.configuration.memoryExtractTimeout: Longest wait (seconds) for the turn-end memory extraction. Title generation, next-step suggestions and memory extraction share one model call at the end of a turn, so the actual timeout is the most generous one among the enabled tasks. Default 90, range 0–600 (0 = no limit).
iflow.configuration.memoryMaintenanceEna: Tidy the managed memory sections (dedupe, merge, archive low-value facts) on a schedule while the panel is idle. Off by default; with the default report strategy it only writes a summary and never modifies a file.
iflow.configuration.memoryMaintenanceInt: How often automatic memory maintenance runs, in days. Default 7, range 1–90.
iflow.configuration.memoryMaintenanceIdl: Only run maintenance after the panel has been idle for this many minutes (no turn streaming, no pending approval or question, no child sessions running). Default 15, range 1–240.
iflow.configuration.memoryMaintenanceGlo: Token budget for the managed section of global memory. When it is exceeded, duplicate and low-value facts are dropped, merged or archived. Default 4000, range 500–50000.
iflow.configuration.memoryMaintenancePro: Token budget for the managed section of each project memory file. Default 2500, range 500–50000.
iflow.configuration.memoryMaintenanceTot: Total token budget across the managed sections of all memory files. When exceeded, curation runs even before the interval elapses (at most once per cooldown of 6 hours or a quarter of the interval, whichever is longer). Default 12000, range 1000–200000.
iflow.configuration.memoryMaintenanceStr: What automatic maintenance does: report only summarises what would change; apply rewrites the memory files (each file is backed up first and skipped when it changed in the meantime). Default report.
iflow.configuration.nextStepTimeoutSecon: Longest wait (seconds) for the turn-end next-step suggestions. Title generation, next-step suggestions and memory extraction share one model call at the end of a turn, so the actual timeout is the most generous one among the enabled tasks. Default 25, range 0–300 (0 = no limit).
iflow.configuration.compressTimeoutSecon: Longest wait (seconds) for compressing a conversation. The default 0 means no limit, since compressing a very large session can legitimately take minutes; when set, a compression that runs over is cancelled with a notice. Range 0–600.
iflow.configuration.autoCompressThreshol: Context occupancy, as a percentage, that triggers auto-compression. Applies only while Auto-compress context is enabled. Default 95, range 50–100.
iflow.configuration.checkpoints.descript: Snapshot the workspace into a private Git repository before each turn, so file changes can be rolled back turn by turn. Your project's own .git is never touched, and folders that are not Git repositories work too. On by default.
iflow.configuration.checkpointMaxFiles.d: Turn snapshots off for a session once its workspace has more files than this, so very large workspaces do not slow the panel down. Default 50000.
Skip files larger than this size (MB) when snapshotting: their changes are left out of rollback and the snapshot repository stays small. Unchanged files are shared across turns, so they are not stored twice. Default 300; 0 = no size limit.
iflow.configuration.checkpointDir.descri: Root folder for checkpoint snapshots. Supports ~ and workspace-relative paths, and each workspace gets its own subfolder. Leave empty to use the default VSCode workspace storage.
iflow.configuration.checkpointMaxTurns.d: How many snapshot turns to keep per session; older snapshots are cleaned up after each new turn. Default 0 = no limit.
Total size cap (MB) for all session snapshots. When exceeded, the least recently used session snapshots are deleted as a whole, and orphaned or corrupt folders are cleaned up too. Default 0 = no limit.
iflow.configuration.qq.enabled.descripti: Whether the QQ remote task channel is enabled. Off by default.
iflow.configuration.qq.allowedUsers.desc: QQ user openids allowed to submit tasks. Each entry is either a bare openid string or an object like { "openid": "...", "note": "..." } to attach a note. Empty by default, so no private-chat task is accepted. These values are identity identifiers — do not commit them to a version-controlled .vscode/settings.json.
iflow.configuration.qq.allowedGroups.des: QQ group openids allowed to submit tasks. Each entry is either a bare openid string or an object like { "openid": "...", "note": "..." } to attach a note. Empty by default, so no group task is accepted. These values are identity identifiers — do not commit them to a version-controlled .vscode/settings.json.
iflow.configuration.qq.workspace.descrip: Workspace folder remote tasks run in. It must be the current workspace root; pointing at any other root makes the QQ service refuse to start. Empty by default (the current workspace root).
iflow.configuration.qq.remotePolicy.desc: How much a remote task may do: readonly, supervised (the default), or trusted.
iflow.configuration.qq.remotePolicy.read: Read-only: the agent may inspect the workspace, but file writes and commands are refused.
iflow.configuration.qq.remotePolicy.supe: Supervised: tool calls need an approval in QQ, and no response within 4 minutes is treated as a denial.
iflow.configuration.qq.remotePolicy.trus: Trusted: tool calls run without a QQ approval. Only use it for a QQ account and group you fully control.
iflow.configuration.qq.maxConcurrentTask: How many remote tasks may run at the same time. Default 2, range 1-10.
iflow.configuration.qq.rateLimitPerMin.d: How many remote tasks are accepted per minute from QQ. Default 6, range 1-60.
iflow.configuration.qq.resultDetail.desc: How much of a task's result is sent back to QQ: summary, standard (the default), or full.
iflow.configuration.qq.resultDetail.summ: A one-line outcome: success or failure plus the changed file count.
iflow.configuration.qq.resultDetail.stan: A short summary with the files touched and the final message.
iflow.configuration.qq.resultDetail.full: The full final reply, up to the QQ message length limit.
iflow.configuration.qq.autoMerge.descrip: Whether a finished remote task's branch is merged automatically. Off by default.
